minutes.summary: The Trust Fund Commission worked through several fund-specific fiduciary matters (Nathaniel Day Poor Fund cy pres filing, American Legion Poor Fund eligibility, gazebo and sidewalk funds) and spent much of the meeting on a dispute with the school department over scholarship and gift funds still held under the town's EIN number rather than turned over to the town treasurer. The commission voted to request a joint meeting with the School Committee to resolve which trust declarations belong to the town versus the school, ratified several backlogged sets of minutes, and voted to resubmit a previously written oversight bylaw for the November 17 special town meeting warrant.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to seek a joint meeting with the School Committee over scholarship and gift funds still held under the town's EIN rather than turned over to the town treasurer.
The commission voted to resubmit its previously written oversight bylaw for the November 17 special town meeting warrant, though the recording could not confirm the vote count.
The commission decided to issue its own written declaration making active-duty American Legion members eligible for the American Legion Poor Fund, without a separate court filing.
Several sets of backlogged meeting minutes flagged by the town clerk's office were ratified.

why_it_matters: Scholarship and gift funds raised for students may be sitting outside the town treasurer's oversight, which is what the requested joint meeting with the School Committee is meant to sort out.
The oversight bylaw headed for the November 17 special town meeting would give the commission more say over how trust and gift funds are managed, a question voters will eventually see on a warrant.
None of this changes a tax bill directly, but it affects who controls charitable and trust money connected to the schools and town property.
